cards.title: The First Spark
cards.flavor: One proton, one electron. Every star started here, and so do you.

cards.title: Noble Debut
cards.flavor: First full shell, zero drama. Light enough to lift balloons, stable enough to shrug off fights.

cards.title: Battery Brawler
cards.flavor: The lightest metal of all. Hands over its lone outer electron to power your phone.

cards.title: Featherweight Frame
cards.flavor: Light, stiff and nearly invisible to X-rays. Small atom, big structural ego.

cards.title: Hardliner
cards.flavor: Boron fibers stiffen tennis rackets and armor. Three outer electrons, all business.

cards.title: Building Block
cards.flavor: Four bonds, endless shapes: graphite, diamond, you. Life runs on carbon.

cards.title: Air Supply
cards.flavor: About 78% of every breath. Its triple bond barely reacts, until it really does.

cards.title: Flame Feeder
cards.flavor: Feeds every fire and every breath. Grabs electrons like it's starving.

cards.title: Electron Thief
cards.flavor: The most electronegative element. It steals electrons from almost anything.

cards.title: Neon Sign
cards.flavor: Glows red-orange under voltage. Its shell is full, so it wants nothing from no one.

cards.title: Salt Half
cards.flavor: Soft enough to cut with a knife. Drop it in water and stand well back.

cards.title: White Flare
cards.flavor: Burns with a blinding white light. Sits at the heart of every chlorophyll molecule.

cards.title: Can-Do Metal
cards.flavor: The most abundant metal in Earth's crust. A thin oxide skin keeps it from corroding.

cards.title: Chip Maker
cards.flavor: Sand by day, microchip by night. Your phone thinks in silicon.

cards.title: Matchstick
cards.flavor: White phosphorus glows in the dark and ignites in air. Red phosphorus lights your matches.

cards.title: Brimstone
cards.flavor: Yellow, smelly and essential. Rotten-egg gas is just sulfur showing off.

cards.title: Pool Patrol
cards.flavor: Keeps pools clean and table salt salty. Always one electron short of a full shell.

cards.title: The Lazy One
cards.flavor: Its name comes from the Greek for 'idle'. Almost 1% of air, and it never reacts.

cards.title: Banana Power
cards.flavor: Hits water with a lilac flame. Your nerves fire on potassium.

cards.title: Bone Builder
cards.flavor: Holds up your skeleton and the White Cliffs of Dover alike.

cards.title: Rare Lightweight
cards.flavor: Scarce but strong: a pinch toughens aluminum bike frames and brightens stadium lamps.

cards.title: Titan
cards.flavor: As strong as many steels at about half the weight. Jet engines and hip implants love it.

cards.title: Tool Steel
cards.flavor: A pinch hardens steel for wrenches and axles. Named after a Norse goddess.

cards.title: Chrome Finish
cards.flavor: That mirror shine on bumpers. Also the 'stainless' in stainless steel.

cards.title: Steel's Sidekick
cards.flavor: Toughens steel and powers alkaline batteries. Quietly everywhere.

cards.title: Iron Core
cards.flavor: Big stars fuse all the way to iron, then collapse. Heavy, stable and red in your blood.

cards.title: Deep Blue
cards.flavor: Gives glass and paint their rich blue. Magnetic, just like its iron neighbor.

cards.title: Plating Pro
cards.flavor: Shrugs off corrosion, so it plates other metals. Magnetic at room temperature.

cards.title: Live Wire
cards.flavor: Carries the world's electricity. Turns green with age, like the Statue of Liberty.

cards.title: Rust Guard
cards.flavor: Coats steel and corrodes first, sacrificing itself to save the iron underneath.

cards.title: Melts in Your Hand
cards.flavor: Melts at about 30 °C, so it turns liquid in your palm. Helps blue LEDs shine.

cards.title: Transistor Pioneer
cards.flavor: The first transistors were made of germanium. Silicon's older sibling.

cards.title: Poisoner's Choice
cards.flavor: Infamous poison, modern semiconductor. Treat it with respect.

cards.title: Moon Element
cards.flavor: Named after the Moon. Turned light into electricity in early photocells.

cards.title: Liquid Red
cards.flavor: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature. Fumes a nasty red-brown.

cards.title: Hidden Gas
cards.flavor: Its name means 'hidden'. A noble gas that flashes white in camera strobes.

cards.title: Atomic Clock
cards.flavor: Keeps precise time in rubidium clocks. Catches fire on contact with air.

cards.title: Red Flare
cards.flavor: Paints fireworks crimson. Chemically a close cousin of calcium.

cards.title: Village Star
cards.flavor: One of four elements named after Ytterby, a single Swedish village.

cards.title: Reactor Armor
cards.flavor: Cubic zirconia sparkles on rings; zirconium alloys wrap nuclear fuel rods.

cards.title: Superconductor
cards.flavor: Niobium magnets steer particle beams at CERN. Cold, strong and quiet.

cards.title: Heat Hardened
cards.flavor: Melts above 2,600 °C. Keeps steel tough when engines run hot.

cards.title: Made, Not Found
cards.flavor: The first element made artificially. Every one of its isotopes is radioactive.

cards.title: Hard Shell
cards.flavor: A hard platinum-group metal that toughens electrical contacts and catalysts.

cards.title: Mirror Coat
cards.flavor: One of the rarest precious metals. Gives jewelry and mirrors a bright, lasting finish.

cards.title: Clean Exhaust
cards.flavor: Scrubs car exhaust in catalytic converters and soaks up hydrogen like a sponge.

cards.title: Silver Lining
cards.flavor: The best electrical conductor of all metals. Shiny, prized and germ-fighting.

cards.title: Yellow Pigment
cards.flavor: Gave painters brilliant yellows. Toxic, so keep your distance.

cards.title: Screen Coat
cards.flavor: Indium tin oxide makes touchscreens conduct. You're touching some right now.

cards.title: Tin Cry
cards.flavor: Bend a tin bar and it 'cries' with a crackle. Solder's longtime ingredient.

cards.title: Ancient Kohl
cards.flavor: Ancient Egyptians lined their eyes with it. Today it helps plastics resist fire.

cards.title: Earth Element
cards.flavor: Named after the Earth itself. Powers thin-film solar panels.

cards.title: Violet Vapor
cards.flavor: Heat it and it skips liquid, turning straight into violet gas. Your thyroid needs a little.

cards.title: Ion Thruster
cards.flavor: Pushes spacecraft through space in ion engines. Noble, heavy and bright in headlights.

cards.title: Time Keeper
cards.flavor: Its atoms define the second. Melts on a warm day and explodes in water.

cards.title: X-Ray Meal
cards.flavor: Barium meals light up your gut on X-rays. Burns green in fireworks.

cards.title: Row Leader
cards.flavor: Opens the lanthanide row. Sharpens camera lenses and fills hybrid-car batteries.

cards.title: Lighter Flint
cards.flavor: Scrape it and it sparks. The most abundant of the rare earths.

cards.title: Green Twin
cards.flavor: Split from its twin neodymium in 1885. Tints glass and glassblower goggles.

cards.title: Super Magnet
cards.flavor: Makes the strongest permanent magnets: earbuds, motors, wind turbines.

cards.title: Promised Fire
cards.flavor: Named after Prometheus. Radioactive and almost absent from Earth's crust.

cards.title: Heatproof Magnet
cards.flavor: Samarium-cobalt magnets keep their pull at temperatures that ruin others.

cards.title: Money Glow
cards.flavor: Glows red under UV light in euro banknotes to help catch fakes.

cards.title: MRI Helper
cards.flavor: Sharpens MRI scans and grabs stray neutrons in nuclear reactors.

cards.title: Green Phosphor
cards.flavor: Makes screens and lamps glow green. Another export of Ytterby village.

cards.title: Hard to Get
cards.flavor: Its name means 'hard to get at'. Keeps magnets strong when motors heat up.

cards.title: Magnetic Peak
cards.flavor: Packs one of the highest magnetic moments of any element. Named for Stockholm.

cards.title: Fiber Booster
cards.flavor: Amplifies light in fiber-optic cables and tints glass pink.

cards.title: Rare Glow
cards.flavor: One of the rarest rare earths. Powers some portable X-ray machines.

cards.title: Clockwork
cards.flavor: Ytterbium atomic clocks are among the most precise clocks ever built.

cards.title: Last Lanthanide
cards.flavor: Closes the lanthanide row. Dense, hard and pricey.

cards.title: Reactor Rod
cards.flavor: Soaks up neutrons in control rods. Found hiding inside zirconium ore.

cards.title: Tantalizing
cards.flavor: Named for Tantalus of Greek myth. Tiny tantalum capacitors live in every phone.

cards.title: Highest Melt
cards.flavor: The highest melting point of any metal, about 3,400 °C. Old light bulbs glowed on it.

cards.title: Jet Alloy
cards.flavor: One of the last stable elements found. Keeps jet turbine blades from sagging in the heat.

cards.title: Densest
cards.flavor: The densest natural element. A one-liter block would weigh over 22 kg.

cards.title: Asteroid Mark
cards.flavor: Rare on Earth, common in asteroids. A thin iridium layer marks the dinosaurs' last day.

cards.title: Catalyst Royalty
cards.flavor: Precious, unreactive and a top-tier catalyst. Rarer than gold.

cards.title: Gold Rush
cards.flavor: Never tarnishes. Earth's gold was forged in violent cosmic events like neutron-star mergers.

cards.title: Quicksilver
cards.flavor: The only metal that's liquid at room temperature. Beautiful, heavy, toxic.

cards.title: Green Twig
cards.flavor: Named for the bright green line in its spectrum. Notoriously toxic.

cards.title: Heavyweight
cards.flavor: Blocks X-rays and radiation. The Romans made water pipes from it, a bad idea.

cards.title: Rainbow Crystal
cards.flavor: Grows iridescent stair-step crystals. Also settles upset stomachs.

cards.title: Curie's Tribute
cards.flavor: Discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie, named for Poland. Intensely radioactive.

cards.title: Rarest Natural
cards.flavor: Perhaps a gram or so exists in Earth's crust at any moment. Gone almost as fast as it forms.

cards.title: Basement Gas
cards.flavor: A radioactive noble gas that seeps out of rock. Test your basement.

cards.title: Fleeting
cards.flavor: The last element found in nature. Its longest-lived isotope lasts about 22 minutes.

cards.title: Glow Paint
cards.flavor: Once painted on watch dials to glow. Discovered by the Curies.

cards.title: Ray Starter
cards.flavor: Opens the actinide row and glows a pale blue in the dark.

cards.title: Thunder Metal
cards.flavor: Named after Thor. A candidate fuel for future nuclear reactors.

cards.title: Before Actinium
cards.flavor: Its name means 'first actinium', because it decays into actinium.

cards.title: Power Core
cards.flavor: Fuels nuclear power plants. The heaviest element found in large amounts in nature.

cards.title: Beyond Uranium
cards.flavor: The first element past uranium, named after the planet past Uranus.

cards.title: Deep Space Battery
cards.flavor: Plutonium-238's heat powers Voyager and the Mars rovers.

cards.title: Smoke Sentinel
cards.flavor: A speck of americium inside smoke detectors keeps watch.

cards.title: Curie's Legacy
cards.flavor: Named for Marie and Pierre Curie. Glows from its own radioactivity.

cards.title: Berkeley Made
cards.flavor: First made at Berkeley in 1949, and named after the city.

cards.title: Neutron Source
cards.flavor: Californium-252 kick-starts reactors and helps find gold and oil.

cards.title: Einstein's Echo
cards.flavor: First found in debris from the first hydrogen bomb test. Named for Einstein.

cards.title: Hundred Club
cards.flavor: Element 100, named for Enrico Fermi. Also first found in H-bomb debris.

cards.title: Table Maker
cards.flavor: Honors Mendeleev, who built the periodic table you're climbing.

cards.title: Nobel Element
cards.flavor: Named for Alfred Nobel. Made only a few atoms at a time.

cards.title: Last Actinide
cards.flavor: Closes the actinide row. Honors Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron.

cards.title: Superheavy Start
cards.flavor: Honors Ernest Rutherford, who discovered the atomic nucleus you're built around.

cards.title: Lab Town
cards.flavor: Named after Dubna, the Russian town where it was made.

cards.title: Living Legend
cards.flavor: Named for Glenn Seaborg while he was still alive, a rare honor.

cards.title: Bohr's Own
cards.flavor: Honors Niels Bohr, whose atom model you are living in right now.

cards.title: Hessian
cards.flavor: Named after the German state of Hesse. Gone in seconds.

cards.title: Meitner's Due
cards.flavor: Honors Lise Meitner, who helped explain nuclear fission.

cards.title: Darmstadt Born
cards.flavor: Made in Darmstadt, Germany. Its atoms last only moments.

cards.title: X-Ray Honor
cards.flavor: Honors Wilhelm Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays.

cards.title: Copernican
cards.flavor: Honors Copernicus. Predicted to be so volatile it might be a liquid or even a gas.

cards.title: Japan's First
cards.flavor: Nihon means Japan. The first element discovered in Asia.

cards.title: Island Seeker
cards.flavor: May sit near the hoped-for 'island of stability' for superheavy atoms.

cards.title: Moscow Made
cards.flavor: Named for the Moscow region. Decays in a fraction of a second.

cards.title: Livermore Lab
cards.flavor: Honors Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. Fleeting and fierce.

cards.title: Tennessee Mystery
cards.flavor: Named for Tennessee. Sits in the halogen column, but too few atoms exist to test it.

cards.title: Final Shell
cards.flavor: The heaviest element ever made. Reach it and the periodic table is complete.
